Flow rate = 29.83 × C × d² × √P — d is the discharge opening's diameter, not the pipe's. C values below are standard NFPA/IFSTA coefficients — match to the opening shape. P is the pitot (velocity) pressure measured at the discharge stream — not a static or residual gauge reading elsewhere in the system, which would give a wrong (often much too high) flow.

OSHA sets no minimum CFM for a space size. It requires “ventilating the permit space as necessary to eliminate or control atmospheric hazards” (29 CFR 1926.1204(c)(4)). This only turns an air-change rate into airflow: CFM = volume × ACH ÷ 60. Take the ACH from the job’s ventilation plan.

Where the ACH presets come from

There is no officially accepted (OSHA) air-changes-per-hour rate. The 20, 40 and 60 ACH presets come from manufacturer guidance (Allegro Industries), a university procedure (MIT) and NIOSH-funded research (Garrison & Erig, 1989, which recommends a 20 ACH minimum for confined-space ventilation design) — sources as listed by the app’s owner. Ventilation never replaces air testing: a gas monitor (sniffer) reading is still required before entry and during entry.
Not a substitute for your safety program
